title: Etale schemes over a field and continuous G-sets
statement: Let K be a field [def-pc-field-extension], K^sep a separable closure, and G=Gal(K^sep/K) with its Krull topology. The functor X \mapsto Hom_K(Spec K^sep,X) is an equivalence from the category of etale K-schemes [def-weil-etale-morphism] to the category of discrete continuous G-sets. Under this equivalence, etale coverings correspond to jointly surjective families of G-equivariant maps.

source.place: Tags 03QR (Lemma lemma-sheaves-point), 03QS (Remark remark-covering-surjective), and 03SF (finite etale objects under a Galois extension); the proof uses Morphisms, Lemma 04HF (etale over a field is a coproduct of finite separable spectra)

proof.text: For an etale K-scheme X, the set Hom_K(Spec K^sep,X) carries a G-action by precomposition. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-etale-fibre-discrete-separable-points] with S=Spec K: X is a disjoint union of spectra of finite separable extensions, so every geometric point factors through one such component. By [lem-exc-etale-field-galois-classification], the stabilizer of a point is Gal(K^sep/sigma(L)) for the corresponding K-embedding sigma, an open subgroup of G. Thus the action is discrete and continuous, and the construction is functorial in X.

proof.text: A morphism of etale K-schemes induces a G-equivariant map on geometric points. Decompose source and target into their connected finite-separable spectrum components by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-fibre-discrete-separable-points] with S=Spec K. On one source component, connectedness forces an equivariant map to land in one target orbit; the full-faithfulness clause of [lem-exc-etale-field-galois-classification] identifies that equivariant map with a unique K-morphism of spectra. Taking these componentwise maps gives a unique K-morphism of the coproducts. Conversely, the same componentwise construction sends every K-morphism to its geometric-point map, so the functor is fully faithful.

source.place: Tag 03QR, Lemma lemma-sheaves-point, full-faithfulness paragraph, using the finite Galois correspondence

proof.text: Let S be a discrete continuous G-set. Decompose S into G-orbits. For s in S, continuity makes its stabilizer G_s open, so the orbit G/G_s is finite; by [lem-exc-etale-field-galois-classification] there is a finite separable extension L_s/K with G_s=Gal(K^sep/L_s), namely L_s=(K^sep)^{G_s}, and the orbit is represented by Spec L_s. Each Spec L_s -> Spec K is etale by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-separable-extension-etale], and their coproduct is etale by [lem-exc-etale-coproduct-etale]. Its geometric points are the disjoint union of the corresponding finite orbits, canonically isomorphic to S. Therefore the functor is essentially surjective.

proof.text: For a family (U_i \to X) of etale morphisms of etale K-schemes, write P(-)=Hom_K(Spec K^sep,-). Suppose the family is a covering in the small etale site, i.e. jointly surjective on points [def-weil-pbc-etale-site]. Let \bar x \in P(X) lie over x in X and pick u in some U_i mapping to x. By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-fibre-discrete-separable-points] with S=Spec K, the components {x} of X and {u} of U_i are isomorphic over K to Spec kappa(x) and Spec kappa(u) with kappa(x), kappa(u) finite separable over K, and the morphism U_i \to X restricts to a K-morphism Spec kappa(u) \to Spec kappa(x). By [lem-exc-etale-field-galois-classification], P(Spec kappa(u)) and P(Spec kappa(x)) are transitive (in particular nonempty) G-sets; the induced G-equivariant map between them hits some point of the transitive G-set P(Spec kappa(x)) and hence, by equivariance, all of it; \bar x factors through the component {x} (Spec K^sep is a single point), so \bar x is hit. Thus the family is jointly surjective on P. Conversely, assume the maps P(U_i) \to P(X) are jointly surjective. For x in X, [lem-weil-pbc-etale-fibre-discrete-separable-points] with S=Spec K says that kappa(x) is finite separable over K, so P(Spec kappa(x)) is nonempty by [lem-exc-etale-field-galois-classification] and x admits a point \bar x in P(X) over it; a preimage of \bar x in some P(U_i) lies over a point of U_i mapping to x. Thus the family is jointly surjective on points, and it is a covering by the definition [def-weil-pbc-etale-site] of coverings in the small etale site. Under the equivalence already established, these are exactly jointly surjective families of G-equivariant maps.
